question: Which station can hold the most bikes?
context:
Database: bike_share (city bike-sharing system)
Table stations: Docking stations where riders pick up and return bikes.
  - station_id INTEGER (primary key)
  - station_name TEXT: Public name of the station.
  - precinct TEXT: City precinct the station sits in.
  - docks INTEGER: Number of docking points installed at the station.
  - status INTEGER: Operating state code: 1 = under construction, 2 = open and in service, 3 = temporarily suspended, 4 = permanently closed.
Table bikes: The fleet of rental bikes.
  - bike_id INTEGER (primary key): Unique bike identifier.
  - fleet_tag TEXT: Fleet number printed on the bike frame.
  - kind INTEGER: Bike category code: 1 = standard pedal bike, 2 = electric-assist bike, 3 = cargo bike.
  - in_fleet_since TEXT: Date the bike joined the fleet, YYYY-MM-DD.
  - odometer REAL: Kilometres ridden since the bike's last depot service; reset to zero at every service.
Table members: Registered riders of the scheme.
  - member_id INTEGER (primary key): Unique member identifier.
  - full_name TEXT
  - suburb TEXT: Suburb where the member lives.
  - plan INTEGER: Subscription code: 1 = pay-per-ride, 2 = monthly pass, 3 = annual pass, 4 = student concession.
  - joined_on TEXT: Date the member signed up, YYYY-MM-DD.
Table trips: Completed rentals, one per ride from unlock to return.
  - trip_id INTEGER (primary key): Unique trip identifier.
  - member_id INTEGER: The member who took the trip.
  - bike_id INTEGER: The bike that was used.
  - start_station_id INTEGER: Station where the bike was unlocked.
  - end_station_id INTEGER: Station where the bike was returned.
  - started_at TEXT: Moment the trip began, as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS in UTC; the city's local time is UTC-5.
  - duration INTEGER: Length of the ride in whole minutes.
  - fare INTEGER: Amount charged for the trip in ride credits; one credit is worth 50 cents.
Table maintenance: Repair jobs logged by the workshop.
  - job_id INTEGER (primary key): Unique repair job identifier.
  - bike_id INTEGER: The bike that was repaired.
  - category INTEGER: Repair type code: 1 = tire or puncture, 2 = brakes, 3 = battery or motor, 4 = chain or gears, 5 = frame or crash damage.
  - reported_on TEXT: Date the fault was reported, YYYY-MM-DD.
  - fixed_on TEXT: Date the repair was completed, YYYY-MM-DD.
  - cost REAL: Total cost of the job, labour and parts, in Canadian dollars.
Foreign keys: trips.member_id -> members.member_id, trips.bike_id -> bikes.bike_id, trips.start_station_id -> stations.station_id, trips.end_station_id -> stations.station_id, maintenance.bike_id -> bikes.bike_id

  - airport_id INTEGER (primary key): Internal number identifying the airport.
  - code TEXT: Three-letter code printed on tickets and boarding passes.
  - city TEXT: City the airport serves.
  - country TEXT: Country where the airport is located.
Table aircraft: One row per aircraft in the fleet.
  - aircraft_id INTEGER (primary key)
  - tail TEXT: Registration mark painted on the aircraft.
  - model TEXT
  - seats INTEGER: Number of passenger seats in the cabin layout.
  - max_range INTEGER: Longest distance the aircraft can fly with a full passenger load, in nautical miles.
  - flight_hours INTEGER: Flight hours logged since the aircraft's last major overhaul.
Table flights: One row per scheduled flight departure.
  - flight_id INTEGER (primary key): Internal number identifying this scheduled departure.
  - flight_no TEXT: Public flight number shown on tickets, reused on later dates.
  - origin_id INTEGER: Airport the flight departs from.
  - dest_id INTEGER: Airport the flight is scheduled to land at.
  - aircraft_id INTEGER
  - departs_at TEXT
  - status INTEGER: Outcome code: 1 = landed at the planned airport, 2 = cancelled, 3 = diverted to another airport.
  - arr_delta INTEGER: Scheduled arrival time minus actual arrival time in minutes, so positive means early and negative means late.
Table passengers: One row per registered passenger.
  - passenger_id INTEGER (primary key): Customer number of the passenger.
  - name TEXT: Passenger full name.
  - nationality TEXT: Nationality shown on the passport.
  - birth_year INTEGER: Year of birth.
  - tier INTEGER: Loyalty programme level: 0 = not a member, 1 = silver, 2 = platinum, 3 = gold.
  - points INTEGER
Table bookings: One row per ticket sold to a passenger for a flight.
  - booking_id INTEGER (primary key): Ticket reference number.
  - passenger_id INTEGER: Passenger the ticket was issued to.
  - flight_id INTEGER
  - cabin INTEGER: Cabin booked: 1 = economy, 2 = business, 3 = premium economy.
  - fare INTEGER: Price paid for the ticket in euro cents, taxes included.
  - channel INTEGER: Sales channel code: 1 = airline website, 2 = mobile app, 3 = travel agency, 4 = call centre.
  - booked_on TEXT: Date the ticket was bought, written as YYYY-MM-DD.

Database: university (university course administration)
Table departments: One row per academic department of the university.
  - dept_id INTEGER (primary key): Identifier of the department.
  - dept_name TEXT: Official name of the department.
  - building TEXT: Building that houses the department office.
  - annual_budget REAL: Yearly operating budget of the department, expressed in thousands of euros.
Table instructors: One row per member of the teaching staff.
  - instructor_id INTEGER (primary key): Identifier of the instructor.
  - instructor_name TEXT: Full name of the instructor.
  - dept_id INTEGER
  - contract_type INTEGER: Employment arrangement code: 1 = permanent post, 2 = fixed-term contract, 3 = adjunct paid per course, 4 = visiting lecturer from another university.
  - hire_year INTEGER: Calendar year in which the instructor was first hired.
Table students: One row per student currently registered at the university.
  - student_id INTEGER (primary key)
  - student_name TEXT: Full name of the student.
  - dept_id INTEGER: Department of the student's declared major.
  - start_year INTEGER: Calendar year in which the student first enrolled at the university.
  - fee_category INTEGER: Fee arrangement code: 1 = standard domestic fee, 2 = international fee, 3 = full scholarship with tuition waived, 4 = staff-dependent discount.
  - account_balance REAL: Current balance of the student's fee account in euros, calculated as payments received minus fees charged, so a negative balance means the student still owes the university.
Table courses: One row per course in the catalogue, each taught by a single instructor.
  - course_id INTEGER (primary key): Identifier of the course.
  - course_title TEXT: Title of the course as shown in the catalogue.
  - dept_id INTEGER: Department that offers the course.
  - instructor_id INTEGER: Instructor who teaches the course.
  - credit_points INTEGER: Credit value of the course in ECTS points, where one point stands for 26 hours of total student work.
Table enrolments: One row per student registration on a course in a given term, with the final grade.
  - enrolment_id INTEGER (primary key): Identifier of the course registration.
  - student_id INTEGER: Student who registered for the course.
  - course_id INTEGER: Course the student registered for.
  - term TEXT: Term code made of the last two digits of the calendar year in which the academic year starts followed by one semester digit (1 = autumn, 2 = spring, 3 = summer session), so 241 is autumn 2024 and 243 is the summer session of 2025.
  - grade INTEGER: Final grade on a 1 to 5 scale where 1 is the best, 4 is the lowest passing grade and 5 means the course was failed.
Table fee_payments: One row per payment received from a student by the bursar's office.
  - payment_id INTEGER (primary key): Identifier of the payment.
  - student_id INTEGER: Student who made the payment.
  - kind INTEGER: Payment purpose code: 1 = tuition instalment, 2 = late-payment penalty, 3 = exam resit fee, 4 = refundable equipment deposit.
  - paid_on TEXT: Date the payment was received, written as DD/MM/YYYY.

  - course_id INTEGER: Course the student registered for.
  - term TEXT: Term code made of the last two digits of the calendar year in which the academic year starts followed by one semester digit (1 = autumn, 2 = spring, 3 = summer session), so 241 is autumn 2024 and 243 is the summer session of 2025.
  - grade INTEGER
Table fee_payments: One row per payment received from a student by the bursar's office.
  - payment_id INTEGER (primary key): Identifier of the payment.
  - student_id INTEGER: Student who made the payment.
  - amount REAL: Amount paid, in euros.
  - kind INTEGER: Payment purpose code: 1 = tuition instalment, 2 = late-payment penalty, 3 = exam resit fee, 4 = refundable equipment deposit.
  - paid_on TEXT
